chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Aban from Yahya al-Azraq, the seller of Sabir, said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'A man performed the Friday prayer and recited "Glory be to the name of his Lord" and "Say: He is Allah, the One".' He said: 'It is sufficient for him.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It is sufficient for him / It fulfills the obligation
key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ: Glory be to the name of his Lord (Surah Al-A'la)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: Is it sufficient to recite Surah Al-A'la and Surah Al-Ikhlas during Friday prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the permissibility of reciting shorter, high-impact Surahs during the Friday prayer, reflecting the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence. The Imam’s affirmation that this combination 'suffices' (ajza-hu) underscores the principle that the spiritual essence of the recitation outweighs length, a view supported by the prominence of these two Surahs in daily devotions. This ruling is particularly significant for congregants who may wish to maintain brevity while ensuring the validity of their obligatory prayer.
